key_insight: EgoGeneralist connects egocentric video with metric 3D human motion in one model. It adapts pretrained video generators to generate video from actions, estimate poses, and generate actions and video together.
problem_solved: Modern video models have strong visual knowledge but lack native representations of human action in metric 3D space, limiting their ability to connect visual generation with precise motion understanding and control.
method: Adapt pretrained video generators for unified egocentric action-video modeling.
Use a role-adaptive action renderer to represent metric motion in a video-native format.
Support action-conditioned video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation, with motion serving as either a control signal or a prediction target.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a unified way to connect video synthesis with 3D motion estimation and control. It could reduce reliance on separate task-specific models, though the provided abstract does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: A central EgoGeneralist model connected to three task icons: action-to-video, video-to-pose, and joint action-video generation.
A pipeline showing a metric 3D skeleton transformed by the action renderer into a video-native representation.
An egocentric video frame paired with a corresponding 3D pose to illustrate the visual-motion connection.
Bidirectional arrows showing motion as both an input control signal and an output prediction target.
paper_title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
paper_authors: Yanlin Jin, Bowen Yang, Cheng Zhang, Yifan Yang, Zhe Li
